name: Carriage Sentry
description: A mobile Q machine follows its owner, then braces for half a second before firing. Shorter range and lost moving fire trade sustained output for relocation.

name: Pressure Charges
description: Q places an armed proximity charge instead of a turret. Up to two charges; one second arming, half-second visible fuse, ordinary control and finite explosions.

name: Anchor Circuit
description: Anchor every carriage, then recall it to follow. Commands share a short recovery and require fresh bracing.

name: Survey Drive
description: Order carriages to a fixed, legal point ahead of your aim. They travel there and hold formation.

name: Coil Lance
description: Earn a fourth active action: a carriage commits its aim, charges, then fires a piercing beam.

name: Prism Coils
description: Coil Lance becomes a three-lane sequence, sweeping a wider approach with separately timed rays.

name: Salvage Pulse
description: Earn a fifth active action: dismantle nearby carriages to recover part of Q deployment cooldown.

name: Rail Convergence
description: All surviving carriages commit converging rails, followed by a warned collapse at their shared mark.

name: Tripwire Couplers
description: Two ready plates share a visible clear tripwire. Crossing it commits both full fuses. Choose this or Safety Switch.

name: Safety Switch
description: Q during deployment cooldown or with both slots full holds or releases idle plates. A committed fuse cannot be interrupted. Choose this or Tripwire Couplers.

name: Firing Key
description: Add action 1: commit every ready owned plate to its full visible fuse, including held plates.

name: Breach Casings
description: Committed explosions also release a warned shaped jet along each plate's placed direction. Cover can shorten the warned lane.

name: Haul Line
description: Add action 2: winch a nearby idle plate to a legal aimed position, then fully rearm it. Its original lifetime remains.

name: Demolition Corridor
description: Remote-fire two clear linked plates, then release a warned demolition strip. Both plates must actually detonate; interrupted ground cancels the strip.

name: Field Screen
description: Q assembles a finite owned screen instead of a turret. It takes half a second to brace; friendly movement remains clear.

name: Longspan Panels
description: Build one broad screen with the same health spread over a longer frontage. Excludes Return Wings.

name: Return Wings
description: Build two angled side screens instead of a flat front. They share the original health budget and leave the central approach exposed. Excludes Longspan Panels.

name: Hinged Assembly
description: Add action1: fold and pivot a nearby owned screen group to a fixed aimed heading. Folded panels cannot block shots.

name: Field Maintenance
description: Add action2: stay still for a committed repair to one damaged owned wall. No player healing, shield or lifetime extension.

name: Linked Foundations
description: Maintain two separate Q screen groups at once. Each keeps its own original lifetime and assembly window.

name: Survey Frame
description: Evolve the hinge action to fold and shift a screen group toward a fixed work point before rebracing. Existing health and expiry remain.

name: Keystone Redoubt
description: Impossible Machine also assembles three finite cover panels on clear ground around its original position. The machine keeps its issued behavior; losing it removes its fortification.

name: Passing Shot
description: After Precision Burst, use action 1 within 1.2 seconds while holding movement: commit a 90-pixel, 0.3-second step and fire a separate 15-base-damage piercing round on arrival. No dodge immunity; blocked ground rejects without spending the opening.

name: Crossing Advance
description: Action 1 commits forward along your aim. Split its original follow-up damage between a departure round and an arrival round; aim again for the arrival shot. You commit the route before moving.

name: Rear Guard
description: Action 1 commits backward from your aim. Fire its original follow-up round halfway through and intercept at most one visible hostile projectile in the short forward lane. Other shots and fixed hazards remain dangerous.

name: Cartridge Drill
description: Earn action 2: load up to four missing rounds individually while walking. Primary fire waits; use action 2 again to stop with completed rounds retained. Fresh burst/step, dodge, ordinary reload or health damage interrupts.

name: Roving Chamber
description: Keep the same finite Cartridge Drill running through fresh Precision Burst and Passing Shot, including either early fork. Coordinate three actions without gaining extra rounds, faster loading or immunity.

name: Ready Round
description: The first actual Cartridge Drill insertion opens a short paid Passing Shot. Spend one magazine round for the existing step shot without a burst opening, while respecting its recovery. A normal ready burst follow-up stays free.

name: Running Volley
description: Spend a loaded step opening during Passing Shot recovery. Once per drill, completing the first paid step and actually inserting three rounds earns a brief second paid step. Each spends one round and keeps the owned movement/fire/guard variant.

name: Bank Shot
description: Spend one magazine round on a deliberate shot that reflects from one masonry face. Plan the angle through real cover; a second wall stops it. Uses action 1 instead of the Skirmisher discipline.

name: Double Bank
description: Carry Bank Shot through a second real masonry contact. Its original lifetime and travel budget stay finite; a third wall absorbs it. Choose this instead of Line Drive.

name: Line Drive
description: After its first real bank, the shot can pass through one ordinary hostile body. Bosses, weak points and further cover still stop it. Bodies before the bank still intercept. Choose this instead of Double Bank.

name: Measured Pair
description: Action 2 spends one actual round on a bank shot and starts twelve seconds of recovery. Its first real cover contact earns 1.2 seconds to manually aim and spend one further round with action 2. At most two shots; the second cannot earn another. Both inherit your chosen bank variant.

name: Held Measure
description: After Measured Pair earns its second shot, begin one real manual Reload to keep that opportunity through the reload and 0.6 seconds afterward, at most four seconds total. It cannot be reserved twice. Dodge, channel, overdrive, weapon or technique loss cancels the reserved opportunity. The normal reload still takes its full time; no extra rounds are created.

name: Angle Relay
description: Only the second paid Measured Pair shot's first real cover bank earns 0.8 seconds for one paid Bank Shot during its recovery. Spend one real round and extend, rather than reset, the existing Bank Shot recovery. An ordinary ready shot consumes the same opportunity. No automatic shot or recursive proof.

name: Twin Lanes
description: When using an earned Angle Relay during Bank Shot recovery, spend two actual rounds to fire two physical bank shots ten degrees to either side of your manual aim. Both inherit your chosen bank variant and use real cover, bodies, travel and armor. Both projectile slots must fit or nothing is spent. One release consumes the relay and extends recovery; neither shot earns another opportunity. Ordinary ready Bank Shot remains one round.

name: Cooked Canister
description: Press action 1 to prepare one canister and start ten-second base recovery. Press again to throw along your manual aim. Its 2.4-second fuse keeps running while held or moving; holding to expiry safely vents the canister and spends the recovery. A normal cast starts at 650 pixels/second, slows on the floor, and stops at bodies or cover before its 90-pixel, 80-base-damage blast. Cover and source-sensitive armor apply. A live hand blocks primary fire until you throw or cancel; firing, Reload, dodge, actual health loss, burst or overdrive interrupts it. No friendly damage, ammunition refill or extra resource. Choose this discipline instead of Skirmisher or Marksman.

name: Skimming Case
description: The thrown canister banks once from real fixed cover, retaining the unused portion of that tick and eighty percent of its speed. A further wall or a body grounds it; the same finite fuse continues. Excludes Contact Case.

name: Contact Case
description: A thrown canister bursts on its first physical body or cover contact instead of waiting on the floor. It cannot bank, seek a target or pass cover. Manual cooking still sets how long it can travel before the fuse expires. Excludes Skimming Case.

name: Underhand Cast
description: Action 2 makes a short cast at 280 pixels/second. It can release the canister already in your hand, or prepare and cast a fresh one in a single press if the same recovery is ready. Floor drag, bodies, cover and the actual remaining fuse still apply; no second stock or recovery is created.

name: Re-pin Drill
description: One Reload press may re-pin a live hand canister for at most four seconds, freeing the hand. The remaining fuse is stored exactly, never rewound. Action 1 resumes that same canister; it may not be re-pinned twice, including after a later catch. Ordinary magazine reload is separate. Excludes Clipped Sling; this preparation choice is optional before Toe Roll.

name: Clipped Sling
description: Keep the live hand canister while using your issued Precision Burst and its owned General transformations. Its fuse keeps running; this grants no burst damage, free ammo or recovery. Primary fire, ordinary Reload, dodge, health loss and overdrive still interrupt it. Excludes Re-pin Drill; this offensive timing choice is optional before Toe Roll.

name: Toe Roll
description: Action 2 near your own grounded canister kicks that actual object along manual aim at 420 pixels/second. You must be within 48 pixels with a clear path. One kick per canister; its remaining fuse, casing choice and spent recovery stay exact. A nearby eligible grounded canister takes priority over a fresh short cast. No teleport, new charge, targeting or fuse refresh.

name: Live Return
description: Action 1 can catch your own grounded canister within 48 clear pixels when at least 0.2 seconds of fuse remains. It returns the same object to your hand for another manually aimed throw. One catch per canister; its remaining fuse, spent kick/re-pin rights, casing and recovery are retained. Pool rejection cannot eat the held charge. No new explosive, stock or rewound clock.

name: Settled Shot
description: Action 1 reserves one actual magazine round and starts ten-second base recovery. Stand still for 0.7 seconds, then press action 1 again to fire a manually aimed, direct 110-base-damage physical shot. Preparation lasts at most three seconds and never fires automatically. Turning more than twelve degrees from the settled bearing recenters the sight and restarts settling within the original deadline. Movement, a new primary press, Reload, dodge, health loss, burst or overdrive cancels the paid preparation without refund. A held primary stays blocked through preparation; release and press it again to cancel. Let an already committed burst finish before preparing. Cover, bodies, travel and source armor apply; no bank, piercing, targeting or immunity. Choose this discipline instead of Skirmisher, Marksman or Grenadier.

name: Careful Carry
description: Movement can carry the same paid Settled Shot round within its original three-second preparation. Every actual displacement moves the sight to your current position, recenters its bearing and restarts the full0.7-second settle. Stop and settle before separately releasing; there is no moving release, extra speed, protection or deadline extension. Fresh preparation still requires a planted body. Reload, dodge, actual health loss, channel, burst, overdrive or a new primary press after release still abandons the round. Choose this handling instead of Clear Chamber.

name: Clear Chamber
description: During valid Settled Shot preparation, press Reload to return exactly its one reserved round into available magazine space. This cancels preparation and keeps the spent recovery; that press clears the chamber rather than starting an ordinary reload. A full magazine rejects the clear and preserves the paid preparation and original deadline. A later Reload without preparation works normally. Firing, expiry, movement or another interruption returns nothing. Choose this handling instead of Careful Carry.

name: Bore Through
description: After preparing and settling Settled Shot, action 2 releases the same paid round with70base ability impact instead of110. It may cross one narrow cover section, at most68pixels along its actual path including the round's width, then retains sixty percent impact. Travel inside cover consumes real time and lifespan; deeper masonry, another solid or the first body stops it. Armor uses your actual firing origin. This is no body piercing, bank, targeting or armor bypass. It cannot prepare a fresh round, extend the original opportunity, return ammunition or reset recovery. Action 1 keeps its direct shot. Careful Carry and Clear Chamber remain optional handling choices.

name: Field Rest
description: With no paid round prepared, action2 sets an empty rest at your actual position and bearing. Remain planted for0.7seconds; moving, taking health loss or another action interrupts unfinished setup. Once settled you may leave, but the rest stays fixed and expires9seconds after planting. Return within6pixels and12degrees: an accepted fresh action1 consumes the rest and reserves one actual round ready for a separate manual release. Normal recovery and actual ammunition still apply; unavailable preparation preserves the rest. Elsewhere action1 retains its ordinary full settling. Action2 recalls an existing empty rest, or uses Bore Through when a paid round is prepared. Carry movement restarts settling; Clear returns only the paid round, never the rest. No automatic shot, targeting, remote origin, cover, protection, extra ammunition or new currency.

name: Prepared Withdrawal
description: Prepare two separate Field Rest positions at least96pixels apart, each with its real settling, manual bearing and original expiry. Both must be settled before a normally available action1 claims the first. Only a successful separate manual release earns one return opportunity at the other original site. Physically return within its local position/bearing limits: action1 may reserve another actual round during recovery, ready for its own separate manual release. That alternate payment extends spent recovery by one ordinary action1 duration. A normally ready claim consumes the same finite opportunity. With no paid preparation, action2 sets a second site only after the first settles and from sufficient distance; nearer action2, two sites or an armed return means recall the plan. Carry still requires new settling after movement; Clear returns only its reserved round and keeps recovery. No site, right or ammunition is restored and a return cannot earn another return. Physical bodies, cover, time and firing-origin armor remain.

name: Flak Round
description: Spend one magazine round to launch a defensive flak shell along your manual aim. Its 0.6-second fuse or first body/cover contact makes one burst at its actual position. After nearby shots move, the 45-pixel burst clears at most three small hostile projectiles with clear line of sight. It deals no body damage and cannot clear large objects, beams, fields or ground attacks. Protection begins only at the burst; earlier hits remain. Moving and Braced Firing are allowed. Reloading, dodging, channeling, overdrive, empty ammunition or a full projectile pool rejects launch without payment. Ordinary primary pauses for the launch. Base recovery is eight seconds.

name: Close Pattern
description: Fit a shorter 0.4-second fuse and a 60-pixel all-around burst. It reaches less distant ground before bursting, but covers every bearing. One magazine round, at most three small hostile shots and the same recovery; real bodies and cover still stop the shell. Choose this fitting instead of Forward Baffle.

name: Forward Baffle
description: Fit a longer 0.8-second fuse and a 90-pixel forward burst within a 70-degree fan. The fan keeps the original firing bearing and leaves a real rear gap. One magazine round, at most three small hostile shots and the same recovery; real bodies and cover still stop the shell. Choose this fitting instead of Close Pattern.

name: Manual Fuze
description: Use action 2 to burst your one actual flying flak shell at its present position. Command it before the original fuse ends; the burst still waits until nearby shots have moved. It cannot act on the launch moment, create another shell or burst, return ammunition or reset recovery. Busy hands reject the command while the original flight and fuse continue. Without a live own shell there is no action to command. Both optional burst fittings retain their actual geometry.

name: Running Fuze
description: Change your first Action 2 command into one early interception pulse while the same paid shell keeps flying. That pulse may clear at most one actual small hostile shot. The original fuse or first body/cover contact later makes the final pulse, using only the unspent part of the original combined three-shot allowance. An empty early pulse uses no interception allowance, but the command is still spent. You cannot command that shell again. No new round, extra carrier, extended fuse or recovery reset. Choose this handling instead of Hanging Fuze; omitting both keeps the original immediate three-shot Manual Fuze.

name: Hanging Fuze
description: Your first Action 2 command arrests the actual shell at its current air position and firing bearing. It does not burst on that command or extend its original fuse. A separate later Action 2 can burst the same shell there; its original fuse or an actual enemy body contact can still end it. The one burst retains the original three-small-shot allowance and real cover. Busy rejection keeps the arrested shell and original deadline. No teleport, attachment, extra round, persistent mine, refund or recovery reset. Choose this handling instead of Running Fuze; omitting both keeps the original immediate Manual Fuze.

name: Seam Fuze
description: While your paid flak shell is still live, press Action 1 again to cut its flight and clear a thin seam along the ground it actually crossed. The seam reaches 9 pixels to either side and uses only the unspent part of that shell’s original three-small-shot allowance. Action 2 keeps your acquired point-burst operation, so choose a narrow line behind the shell or a wider burst at it. Running Fuze spends from the same allowance; Hanging Fuze retains only the line laid before arrest. Real cover crossing that line permanently severs it for this shell, leaving Action 2 and the original fuse available. Cut before the original fuse ends. Busy hands reject without cutting. No extra round, body damage, shield, recovery reset or lingering trap.

name: Traverse Stroke
description: Start a finite four-round firing stroke with Action 1. The first physical round leaves immediately; three later rounds each require and spend their own actual magazine round over the next second. Walking pauses while the barrel slews toward manual aim, within sixty degrees of its first bearing. Every admitted round recoils your body eight pixels over the following four combat steps, with real cover blocking movement. Another separate Action 1 releases the feed and lets you walk; fired rounds and their recoil remain. Reload, dodge, channeling or overdrive stops unpaid future rounds. Empty or full-pool rejection spends nothing; a failed later slot ends the feed. Primary waits through the stroke. Each round deals 45 base weapon-scaled damage through ordinary bodies, cover, time and armor. Eight-second base recovery starts with the first admitted round. Choose Siege Gunner instead of Flak Gunner.

name: Set Spade
description: Plant this carriage on stable ground before starting a Traverse Stroke: walking input rejects the start without payment. The stroke adds no recoil and keeps its manual barrel slew, while holding walking input. Any actual external ground displacement breaks the post and ends unpaid future rounds; fired rounds remain. Terrain, moving cover and forced movement still apply. The same four actual rounds, original stroke slots and recovery remain. Choose this fitting instead of Floating Cradle.

name: Floating Cradle
description: Walk normally during a Traverse Stroke and retain each paid round’s actual recoil. Every round keeps the initial world bearing: later mouse aim cannot steer the barrel. Relocate the actual muzzle to find new clear lanes, or release the feed when that bearing becomes useless. This grants no movement bonus, protection or extra round and changes no original stroke slots or recovery. Choose this fitting instead of Set Spade.

name: Feed Clutch
description: After the first paid Traverse round, a separate Action 2 lifts its feed and frees walking immediately. Original firing slots keep passing: each slot crossed while lifted is lost without firing or spending a round. A separate later Action 2 re-engages the remaining original slots. Use one lift and re-engage pair per stroke; neither command adds a round, catches up a missed slot, extends the one-second stroke or resets recovery. Primary still waits while future stroke work remains. Set Spade deliberately lifts its post and requires stationary input to replant at the actual new body point; an already broken post cannot be rescued. Floating Cradle keeps its original world bearing. Paid recoil remains physical while lifted. Action 1 still abandons all unpaid work. Reload, dodge, channeling and overdrive end unpaid work. No fitting is required.

name: Keyed Clutch
description: While Feed Clutch is lifted, manually crank the real barrel within its original sector and slew speed, including a Floating Cradle. Your separate re-engagement keys its actual current bearing for every remaining original C slot; later aim cannot steer it. Loose and Set Spade can aim their issued Suppressing Cone elsewhere but give up later barrel tracking. Floating gains this one bounded calibration window before keeping the new world bearing as it walks. Primary still waits throughout retained C work. Lifting still loses slots that pass unpaid; neither command adds a round, snaps the barrel to the cursor, catches up a missed slot or changes deadline/recovery. Choose this handling instead of Open Feed; omitting both keeps the original Clutch handling.

name: Open Feed
description: Ordinary primary can fire while Feed Clutch is lifted. Each actually admitted and paid primary round consumes the earliest remaining original C opportunity once, regardless of its number of pellets. It spends real magazine ammunition at the issued primary cadence; the complete real volley must fit capacity before any payment. Empty, busy or capacity rejection converts no slot. Re-engagement keeps only the unconverted original C times; slots passed while lifted are still lost unpaid. This trades later committed C fire for earlier ordinary fire while walking, without reserving or refunding rounds, adding a C slot, extending the stroke or resetting recovery. A simultaneous Action 1 still cancels all unpaid C work first. Choose this handling instead of Keyed Clutch; omitting both retains primary commitment during the original Clutch.

name: Tethered Traverse
description: After lifting and re-engaging the feed, press Action 2 separately again to stake this same gun at its actual muzzle and bearing, with at least two original firing opportunities left. Walk within its 64 px control lead while remaining original rounds still pay and travel from that fixed muzzle. Cover cutting the lead, leaving its reach or interruption ends unpaid work. Action 1 releases the stroke. An admitted Suppressing Cone retrieves the gun before firing from your body. No extra round, resource, deadline, recovery reset or autonomous weapon is added.

name: Anchor Cartridge
description: Action1 spends one magazine round on a real900px/s,radius3 anchor with20flight ticks. Current masonry within600px may hold it; living bodies and temporary constructs stop it without becoming attachments. A later separate Action2 engages or brakes the hauling motor. Action1 releases the line. Bare hauling permits lateral walking but commits primary fire. The carried gun stays with your body; current collision, slows and hazards remain. The line lasts150combat ticks from cast, with8second base recovery from payment. A miss still spends the admitted round. Choose Lineworker instead of Flak or Siege Gunner.

name: Straight Yoke
description: While hauling, permit ordinary paid primary and restrict ordinary walking to the current anchor approach axis. Aim every shot yourself. A separate Action2 brakes the motor and restores ordinary steering; another engages within the same remaining line. The original one-round anchor,150tick lifetime,600px maximum and recovery remain. Losing this fitting after using its handling releases dependent work. Choose Straight Yoke instead of Open Sheave.

name: Open Sheave
description: While braked, pay out actual clear cable up to its original600px maximum, then use a separate Action2 to haul from the changed approach. Keep lateral walking while hauling and keep primary fire committed. Repeated braking never resets the original150tick lifetime, returns the paid anchor round or resets recovery. Losing this fitting after using payout releases dependent work. Choose Open Sheave instead of Straight Yoke.

name: Reserve Anchor
description: While braked on an attached line, Action 3 spends one more magazine round on a second physical anchor. It must attach to current masonry at least 100 px from the first contact. A separate Action 3 selects the reserve and releases the first line. Action 2 then hauls on the selected line. Both anchors share the first cast’s expiry and recovery. A paid shot can miss or hit an obstruction. You can prepare one reserve per first anchor.

name: Corner Guide
description: With an attached line braked, stand still and aim at a nearby masonry corner or wall face. Action 3 spends one magazine round to fit a guide. Both cable segments must stay clear and fit the paid cable. Walk the detour, then use Action 2 to haul back to the guide. A separate Action 3 redirects to the original anchor. Action 2 starts the second haul. One guide per first anchor, within its original lifetime and recovery.

name: Shoulder Wall
description: Approach the rear of your Protective Wall. Action 1 folds it into a narrow shield and carries it at the original heading. Walk it across the line of fire. A separate Action 1 sets it down at full width on clear ground. It keeps the same remaining health and expiry. Both hands are occupied until set down.

name: Braced Pivot
description: While carrying and standing still, Action 2 commits the shield toward the aimed bearing over 0.4 seconds. Walking or forced movement interrupts the turn. The shield keeps its original health and expiry. Recovery lasts 2 seconds. Excludes Firing Port.

name: Firing Port
description: While carrying and standing still, Action 2 opens a narrow firing port over 0.2 seconds. Enemy rounds can enter immediately. Aim within 10 degrees of the original bearing to fire paid primary rounds; wide pellets can strike the rim. Another Action 2 closes it over 0.2 seconds. Walking or forced movement closes it and blocks primary fire. Action 1 attempts full-width setdown. Original health, expiry and ammunition remain. Excludes Braced Pivot.

name: Interception Line
description: Action 3 captures a bearing and prepares a screen over 0.2 seconds while you stand still. Release and press Action 3 again to charge behind it, spending Rescue Charge recovery. Your hands stay occupied during the screen. Trade charge impact, new invulnerability and Wake Guard for front projectile cover. E remains the original Rescue Charge. Another Action 3 brakes without a recovery refund.

name: Crossing Guard
description: Keep the captured screen facing and hold sideways movement on the second Action 3 to cross the firing lane. With no movement, retain the forward screen. The complete body and screen route must be clear. Spend the same E recovery and brief window; gain no charge impact or new invulnerability. Excludes Standfast.

name: Standfast
description: The second Action 3 braces the captured screen in place. Walking or another Action 3 ends it. Forego all charge movement, impact, new invulnerability and primary fire to hold a brief front screen. Spend the same E recovery with no refund or extended window. Excludes Crossing Guard.

name: Gate Signal
description: Stand still and aim toward danger with your hands clear. Action 2 spends The City Holds recovery to mark a retreat behind you. Walk from the arrow side across the sill to take the guard. The reserve and guard expire at the original cast deadline.

name: Split Watch
description: Divide the sill into two marked halves. Each half holds half the guard and can serve one crossing. The center divider separates the routes. Excludes Corner Post.

name: Corner Post
description: Mark two perpendicular ways into one reserve. Either open face can grant the whole guard. Both approaches need clear ground. Excludes Split Watch.

name: Relief Watch
description: Stand just behind the spent half of your Split Watch and face danger. Action 2 moves the remaining half guard to this lane once. A real crossing still claims it before the original deadline.

name: Countermarch
description: Stand just behind an open Corner Post approach and aim opposite its original danger side. Action 2 reverses that arrow once. The perpendicular entrance and original reserve share the same deadline.

name: Folded Setdown
description: When terrain blocks a full-width setdown, stand still and use Action 1 to leave the shield folded. It keeps its current health and expires on schedule. You can use your weapon again. The folded shield stays fixed until it breaks or expires.

name: Side Port
description: With the port open, stand still, aim 12 to 35 degrees off center and use Action 2 to move the slit once. Keep still for 0.2 seconds. The old slit stays open during the shift. Aim along the new opening to fire using your ammunition.

name: Return Crossing
description: During a sideways Crossing Guard, use Action 3 with the opposite sideways direction to turn back once. Keep the captured facing and original screen deadline. The return route needs clear ground. Action 3 without that direction brakes.

name: Offset Brace
description: When Standfast is ready, give Action 3 a sideways direction relative to your facing. A narrower screen braces farther out on that side and leaves your center exposed. Stay planted to keep it through its original deadline.

name: Field Dressing
description: Stand still with your hands free. Aim at a nearby ally or away from allies to treat yourself with Action 1. Give up to three quick doses. The first dose spends Healing Field recovery. Moving, another action, lost reach or health loss interrupts treatment.

name: Steady Step
description: After the first Field Dressing dose, walk up to 32 pixels while continuing the treatment. Follow the same patient within reach. Firing, dodging or taking health damage ends treatment. Excludes Set Aside.

name: Set Aside
description: After a Field Dressing dose, press Action 1 while still to set aside one remaining dose. Move or act for up to 0.8 seconds, then stand still and press Action 1 again to treat the same patient within reach. The original recovery still applies. Excludes Steady Step.

name: Tie Off
description: After a paid dose and 5 pixels of Steady Step, use Action 1 while walking to tie off the next dose. You can act while the same patient stays within 24 pixels of the tie point and within treatment reach. Give up any later dose.

name: Wrapped Dressing
description: Halfway through preparation, use Action 1 while still to wrap the dressing. Move or act for up to 0.8 seconds, then stand still and use Action 1 to continue preparation on the same patient. The first successful dose spends Healing Field recovery.

name: Rescue Run
description: Use Action 2 with a clear step ahead while moving to spend Cleansing Serum recovery. Steer the brief run yourself. Cover 48 pixels, stop, and use Action 2 for one focused dose on an aimed ally or yourself. Hold Revive in reach for an ordinary rescue.

name: Switchback
description: After 36 pixels of Rescue Run, use Action 2 while taking a turn of at least 60 degrees. A clear turn buys a quarter-second of extra running once. Excludes Moving Handoff.

name: Moving Handoff
description: After 48 pixels of Rescue Run, aim at a nearby ally or away for yourself and use Action 2 while still moving. Give one smaller dose immediately and end the run. Excludes Switchback.

name: Precaution Wrap
description: Stand still and use Action 3 to prepare one living patient for 2.2 seconds. The first hostile projectile, charge contact or Stitchwright seam that takes health from the patient spends Healing Field recovery and schedules a small follow-up dose. Casting Healing Field ends any unused wrap.

name: Doorstep Kit
description: Prepare yourself, then use Action 3 while standing on clear ground to leave the same wrap at your feet. The first living player to walk in from outside takes it. The original deadline follows the wrap. Excludes Layered Wrap.

name: Layered Wrap
description: Use Action 3 again while the same patient is within reach. The wrap can record two separate qualifying wounds. Stand still within reach and use Action 3 before expiry to schedule a single dose based on the wounds so far. The first wound spends the original recovery. Excludes Doorstep Kit.

name: Pivot Sigil
description: Stand still and aim at clear floor. Use Action 1 to mark a pivot. Stand within clear reach and press again to spend Binding Sigil recovery. Aim to guide the line for a moment. It stops at walls, hits each enemy once and briefly slows ordinary minions. Firing, dodging or casting ends the guided line.

name: Fixed Angle
description: Turn the live line by about 23 degrees, then stand still and use Action 1 to fix the line in place. The same stroke stays until its original deadline while you act or move. Excludes Reverse Face.

name: Reverse Face
description: After turning the line by about 36 degrees, stand still, aim at its opposite face and use Action 1. The line moves there once and keeps its remaining time, turn allowance and earlier contacts. Excludes Fixed Angle.

name: Waymark Return
description: Set a waymark at your feet with Action 2. Walk a clear trail away. Stop and press again to spend Ward Detonation recovery and follow the same trail back. You can still take hits on the way. A new movement order or committed action ends the return.

name: Hold the Trace
description: Travel partway back, then use Action 2 to hold the return briefly in place. You can fire or cast Binding Sigil there. Use Action 2 again to resume once before the hold ends. Both legs keep the original deadline. Excludes Side Landing.

name: Side Landing
description: Near the end of a return, aim across the trail into clear space and use Action 2. The last part bends there once, with the original time and the remaining distance budget. Excludes Hold the Trace.

name: Fuse Seal
description: Plant a seal on clear floor with Action 3. Spend Binding Sigil or Ward Detonation near it to charge a forward or transverse stroke and commit Silent Twelfth recovery. Charge the other spell on a later beat to combine the strokes and shorten the fuse. Aim and use the same action while still to release. A wound takes time off the fuse.

name: Shunt Fuse
description: Walk away from a single-charge seal, then press Action 3 while walking to shift it once to the clear floor under you. The shift takes time off the same paid fuse. Stop and aim to release. Excludes Twin Vent.

name: Twin Vent
description: Feed both spells on different beats. Release each stroke separately in the order you charged them. Aim again for the second stroke before the same fuse expires. Each target can take only one hit across both strokes. Excludes Shunt Fuse.

name: Called Opening
description: Use Action 1 while still to mark one visible enemy. Walk sideways past one shoulder while keeping the target in view. Stop, aim at that enemy and press again to spend Shadow Step recovery on a single strike.

name: Passing Cut
description: After earning the opening, aim and press Action 1 during another real sideways step in the same direction. The strike spends Shadow Step recovery and preserves your walking pace. Excludes Counterturn.

name: Counterturn
description: After earning the opening, walk the other way and press Action 1 to turn back. Walk partway across your old line, then stop and strike the same enemy before the original clock ends. Excludes Passing Cut.

name: Slip Route
description: Face nearby cover while a hostile can see you. Press Action 2 to spend Invisibility recovery. Walk until the cover screens your route. Stop and press again to trade part of the remaining veil for a damageable echo at the entrance.

name: Footstep Relay
description: After you trade veil for an echo, press Action 2 again to send that same body along part of your walked route. It moves through clear ground and keeps its remaining health and expiry. Excludes Threshold Echo.

name: Threshold Echo
description: At the walked exit, press Action 2 to watch the route entrance. A hostile crossing into its clear threshold wakes the echo. Stay within range and press again to release it early. Excludes Footstep Relay.

name: Crossing Writ
description: Mark a visible enemy with Action 3. Land two separate primary hits to confirm it. Aim and press again to spend Unwritten Passage recovery on a cutoff. The marked enemy must cross the line before it expires.

name: Canted Cutoff
description: After confirming the writ, press Action 3 to pin a nearby point. Aim independently and press again to pay for the line before the same mark expires. Excludes Transfer Writ.

name: Transfer Writ
description: While the paid cutoff is live, aim at a new visible enemy and press Action 3. One fresh primary hit confirms the transfer. The same line and deadline carry over. Excludes Canted Cutoff.

name: Call and Response
description: Earn two cadence. Aim at clear ground and press Action 1 to spend Resolving Phrase recovery and your cadence. A call sounds at your feet. Hit an enemy with a primary note fired from the marked stage, then press again to answer there.

name: Side Stage
description: Earn one fresh cadence after the call. Aim to one side and press Action 1 to move the same reply stage. A new primary note must land before the original deadline. Excludes Reprise.

name: Reprise
description: After a note confirms the reply, face the original call site and press Action 1 to send the reply back there. Aim elsewhere to answer from the marked stage. Excludes Side Stage.

name: Mourning Measure
description: Earn two cadence. Aim along clear ground and press Action 2 to spend Cut In recovery and lay a lane. Stay near its start and face along it for up to five pulses. Your primary rests during the measure. Press again to end it early.

name: Cross Verse
description: After the first pulse, aim a little to one side and press Action 2 to turn the same lane once. The turn spends one remaining pulse. The lane keeps its original start and deadline. Excludes Closing Chord.

name: Closing Chord
description: After two damaging pulses, press Action 2 while facing down the lane to play one chord at its far end. It spends all remaining pulses. Excludes Cross Verse.

name: False Entrance
description: Earn two cadence. Aim at clear floor and press Action 3 to mark a false entrance for a few seconds. Walk away from the call to arm it. One nearby ordinary enemy already pursuing you can follow the mark briefly. It still hits players it reaches.

name: Wrong Door
description: While a pursuer follows the mark, aim at a different clear entrance and press Action 3. Spend one fresh cadence to turn that same pursuer within the original window. Excludes Second Entrance.

name: Second Entrance
description: After the first pursuer reaches the mark, press Action 3 to spend one fresh cadence. The same mark can draw one different ordinary enemy before it closes. Excludes Wrong Door.
